::: {#exm-bfs-tree}
#### A breadth-first search tree of the town graph

Give the town graph (@exm-spanning-tree) the adjacency list in which each list is in alphabetical order:

$$
\ba
a &: b, f, g
& b &: a, c
& c &: b, d, g
& d &: c, e
\\ e &: d, f, g
& f &: a, e
& g &: a, c, e
\ea
$$

Then `bfs` (@def-bfs) from $a$ runs as follows:

| Removed $v$ | Newly marked $u$, with `dist[u]` | $Q$ after the pass |
|:-----------:|:-----------------------:|:------------------:|
| $a$ | $b$ (1), $f$ (1), $g$ (1) | $b, f, g$ |
| $b$ | $c$ (2) | $f, g, c$ |
| $f$ | $e$ (2) | $g, c, e$ |
| $g$ | none | $c, e$ |
| $c$ | $d$ (3) | $e, d$ |
| $e$ | none | $d$ |
| $d$ | none | empty |

The breadth-first search tree (@def-bfs-tree) from $a$ has the six edges

$$
\set{a, b}, \set{a, f}, \set{a, g}, \set{b, c}, \set{f, e}, \set{c, d},
$$

drawn thick in @fig-hub-bfs.
With root $a$, its levels are the distances from $a$, as @thm-bfs-tree says:
$b$, $f$ and $g$ are at level 1, $c$ and $e$ at level 2, and $d$ at level 3.
It is a different spanning tree from the one of @exm-spanning-tree.

::: {#fig-hub-bfs}
